title: Care Center Desk Reference: The Kinds of Withdrawal Taken From a Certificate of Deposit Before Maturity
content:
Money leaving a certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line before its maturity date falls into one of several kinds, and the kind decides whether a penalty attaches.

## 1. The certificate's standing

Principal can be withdrawn before maturity only from a certificate whose status is active. The status is read from the certificate record.

The clause under which the withdrawal was taken up as a standing instruction of the owner, recorded in a pending state and carried out only once the owner confirmed it separately, is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis on which such a withdrawal is given effect.

## 2. The order in which the kind is decided

The kind is settled in this order, and the first that fits governs.

1. A withdrawal of interest already credited in the current term, up to the interest credited in that term, is a withdrawal of interest and carries no penalty on a tier that allows credited interest to be withdrawn penalty-free. The interest credited in the term is the interest compounded into the certificate since the term start, less any interest already withdrawn in the term.
2. After the owner's death or court-adjudicated incompetence, confirmed by the bank's estate services, the withdrawal is taken under the waiver and carries no penalty on a tier that grants that waiver.
3. On a tier that publishes a waiting period after which a full withdrawal carries no penalty, a full withdrawal made after that period is penalty-free.
4. Every other withdrawal before maturity is a full or a partial early withdrawal and carries a penalty.

## 3. The waiting period on a tier that publishes one

A penalty-free withdrawal is allowed only after the calendar days the tier publishes have passed since the certificate was funded. Days are counted with the day after the term start date as day 1, and the withdrawal is penalty-free when the current date is on or after the term start date plus that number of days plus one further day. The term start date is read from the certificate record.

*Boundary, on hypothetical dates:* an 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate funded on 4 March publishes 6 days. On 10 March a full withdrawal is not yet penalty-free; on 11 March it is, and on any later day of the term it remains so.

## 4. Limits on taking part of the principal

A partial withdrawal is allowed only on a tier that permits one, for at least the smallest partial withdrawal the tier accepts, leaving at least the balance the tier requires to remain, and no more than the number of early partial withdrawals the tier allows in a term, counted over the withdrawals taken since the term start. A request that breaks any of these is declined; it is never converted into a withdrawal of another kind or size.

## 5. Where the proceeds go

Proceeds go by one of the ways the tier publishes, to an account of the same customer or by an official check.

superseded_clauses: Taking money out of a certificate before maturity is the owner's own decision: the agent registers a cd_requests row of request_type early_withdrawal in pending_customer_confirmation status, and nothing is withdrawn until the owner confirms.
